g.title: G
cluster_micro
cluster_meso
cluster_macro

p1_micro_new_exposure_flag → p1_meso_band_hazard_dispersion upward If new exposures concentrate in some age bands, between-band exposure hazards diverge, increasing cross-band dispersion even when total exposure activity is unchanged.

p1_micro_new_exposure_flag → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge upward More per-agent new-exposure transitions raise the flow of exposure events that can be attributed to contact layers, so layer-level incidence per recorded edge can rise when these transitions cluster in a layer rather than being diffuse.

p1_micro_new_exposure_flag → p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction upward New household exposures increase the chance that a household-layer dyad accumulates at least one attributed exposure, lifting the fraction of dyads with any attributed event.

p1_micro_new_exposure_flag → p4_meso_group_silent_share upward Cohorts of new exposures later enter infectious states; if they are distributed unevenly across quarantine-status groups, the silent share of infectious person-steps in those groups can shift after the exposure-to-infectious delay.

p1_micro_new_exposure_flag → p7_meso_layer_exposure_share upward New exposures that are layer-attributed alter relative layer composition; an increase in exposures in one setting raises its share of attributed transitions.

p1_micro_new_exposure_flag → p8_meso_layer_post_trough_incidence_ratio upward Post-trough new exposures feed layer-attributed incidence after the trough; if they occur preferentially in a layer, that layer's after-versus-at-trough incidence ratio rises.

p1_micro_ever_exposed_state → p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth upward Accumulated ever-exposed state among agents reduces susceptible recruitment after the trough, limiting the aggregate post-trough growth rate of infectious agents.

p1_micro_ever_exposed_state → p8_macro_resurgence_amplitude upward Greater cumulative individual exposure leaves fewer susceptible agents available to fuel a rebound, damping the post-trough resurgence amplitude.

p1_micro_ever_exposed_state → p8_macro_trough_susceptible_depletion upward Agents becoming ever-exposed earlier deplete the local susceptible pool, so the aggregate susceptible share remaining at the city infectious trough is lower.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge upward Higher per-agent contact degree in a layer increases exposure opportunities along recorded edges, raising the layer-level exposure incidence per edge.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p2_meso_layer_active_run upward Agents with many contacts in a layer can sustain transmission chains across consecutive sampled steps, lengthening the layer's active exposure run.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p2_macro_layer_incidence_entropy upward Heterogeneous per-agent degree across layers concentrates exposure activity in high-degree settings, shifting the cross-layer entropy of attributed exposures.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p7_macro_layer_composition_drift upward When individual contact degree grows unevenly across layers, the layer composition of attributed exposures drifts away from its early-run reference.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth upward High per-agent layer degree preserves transmission opportunities after the trough, supporting faster aggregate growth of infectious agents.
p2_micro_layer_degree → p8_macro_resurgence_amplitude upward Higher individual contact degree provides more channels for renewed transmission, increasing the size of the post-trough rebound.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p8_macro_resurgence_breadth upward Agents with contacts spread across layers can seed post-trough increases in multiple settings, broadening the share of layers with resurgence.

p2_micro_layer_beta_load → p1_meso_band_attack_ratio upward Agents carrying larger per-layer contact-weight loads are more likely to generate new exposures through their setting-specific contacts; if this load is unevenly distributed across ages, the affected age bands can accumulate higher attack ratios over the run.

p2_micro_layer_beta_load → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion upward High contact-weight load within a layer makes repeated exposure between connected agents more likely; in the household-like layer this can produce additional secondary events in some dyads and increase dyad-level dispersion of attributed secondary counts.

p3_micro_household_degree → p1_meso_band_attack_ratio upward Higher household-layer degree for an agent increases repeated close-contact exposure within the household setting; when such agents are concentrated in particular age bands, sustained household transmission can raise those bands' cumulative attack ratios rather than merely reflecting a precomputed aggregate.

p3_micro_household_degree → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion upward An agent with more household-layer contacts participates in more dyadic pairs that can receive secondary exposure; variation in household degree therefore changes how unevenly attributed secondary events are distributed across household dyads.

p3_micro_household_degree → p6_meso_quarantined_degree_dispersion upward Agents with large household-layer degree retain more recorded contacts even while quarantined; heterogeneity in household degree among quarantined agents therefore contributes to wider dispersion of observed contact degree in the quarantined subgroup.

p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag → p1_meso_band_hazard_dispersion upward Attributed exposures concentrated among particular ages can widen band-specific exposure hazards, raising cross-band dispersion.

p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge upward Source-attributed exposures are the events entering layer incidence numerators; more attributed exposures per edge raise layer incidence, especially when attribution is concentrated in a layer.

p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag → p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction upward Source-attributed household exposures add dyads to the ever-attacked set, increasing the fraction of household dyads with any attributed exposure.

p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag → p4_meso_group_silent_share upward Attributed exposures seed later infectious individuals; uneven attribution across quarantine-status groups can change the silent share after progression to infectiousness.
p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag → p7_meso_layer_exposure_share upward Attributed exposures determine which layers receive incident events; a shift toward one layer raises its exposure share.

p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag → p8_meso_layer_post_trough_incidence_ratio upward Attributed exposures after the trough drive layer-specific post-trough incidence; concentration in a layer raises its post-trough ratio relative to the trough.

p3_micro_household_attributed_flag → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion upward Repeated household-attributed exposures concentrate in a subset of dyads, increasing dispersion of cumulative attributed exposures across household dyads.

p3_micro_household_attributed_flag → p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction upward Individual household-attributed exposure events convert previously unaffected household dyads into attacked dyads, raising the fraction of dyads with any attributed exposure.

p3_micro_household_attributed_flag → p7_macro_layer_composition_drift upward More household-attributed individual exposures raise the household layer's share of attributed exposures, shifting layer composition over time.

p3_micro_household_attributed_flag → p8_macro_resurgence_amplitude upward Household-attributed exposure chains can persist through low-incidence periods and reseed transmission, increasing post-trough rebound amplitude.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard upward Silently infectious agents remain in contact and contribute infection pressure in their age bands, raising the band-level exposure hazard.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge upward Silent infectious agents active in contact layers generate exposures along recorded edges, increasing layer exposure incidence per edge.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p4_macro_detection_coverage_rate upward A larger silent infectious pool lowers the number of new diagnoses per infectious person-step, reducing observed detection coverage.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p4_macro_masking_ratio upward Silent infectious episodes accumulate undiagnosed ever-exposed agents, increasing the ratio of never-diagnosed to ever-diagnosed infections.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p5_macro_quarantine_coverage upward Undiagnosed silent infectious agents are less likely to be quarantined, lowering population quarantine coverage relative to observed infections.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p6_macro_contact_volume_change upward Silent infectious agents continue normal activity, attenuating the population-wide decline in contact volume after interventions.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p7_macro_growth_change_at_first_quarantine upward Ongoing silent transmission offsets the growth reduction expected around quarantine onset, weakening the observed before-after growth contrast.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth upward Silent infections surviving the trough continue generating new infections, raising post-trough growth of the infectious population.
p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p8_macro_resurgence_amplitude upward Hidden infectious activity provides a reservoir that can seed a larger rebound after the observed infectious minimum.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_duration → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard upward Agents with longer cumulative silent infectious duration continue to contact others while undiagnosed, increasing the rate at which susceptible age-band members become exposed; this raises the band-level exposure hazard beyond what would occur if silent infectious periods were shorter.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_duration → p2_meso_layer_active_run upward Silent infectious agents sustain contact activity in their settings, so layers with such agents experience repeated exposure events across consecutive steps, lengthening the layer's consecutive active-step run.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_duration → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count upward In a household dyad, a silently infectious index case with longer duration has more opportunities to expose the partner, increasing the dyad's attributed secondary exposure count.

p4_micro_symptomatic_undiagnosed_flag → p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion upward Undiagnosed symptomatic agents remain in contact networks and can later be linked to known-contact tracing in different settings; if they are unevenly distributed across layers, the resulting per-index contact load becomes more dispersed across layers.

p4_micro_symptomatic_undiagnosed_flag → p7_meso_band_exposure_share upward Symptomatic-but-undiagnosed agents continue normal social contact without entering surveillance; if this state is more common in some age groups, those groups contribute disproportionately to new exposure transitions and shift the age-band composition of incident exposure activity.

p5_micro_known_contact_flag → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard upward Being flagged as a known contact typically triggers quarantine and reduced social activity, which lowers the exposure hazard in the agent's age band by removing potential transmitters from contact networks.

p5_micro_known_contact_flag → p2_meso_layer_active_run upward Known-contact flags lead to quarantine, reducing the number of active transmitters in contact layers and thereby shortening the layer's consecutive run of exposure events.

p5_micro_known_contact_flag → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count upward When a household member is flagged as a known contact and quarantined, secondary exposures within that dyad are reduced, lowering the dyad's attributed secondary count.

p5_micro_known_contact_flag → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load upward Known-contact flags are the trigger for quarantine; the layer-specific contact degree of newly quarantined flagged agents defines the tracing workload per index, so more flagged agents in a layer increase the layer's per-index contact load.

p5_micro_tracing_latency → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion upward Longer delay from known-contact flag to quarantine leaves source agents and their household contacts active for more steps; this can create additional secondary exposure events in some household dyads and increase dispersion of attributed counts across dyads.

p5_micro_tracing_latency → p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion upward When individual tracing delays are long and uneven, newly quarantined index agents may accumulate different numbers of active layer contacts before isolation; this uneven accumulation can widen the cross-layer dispersion of per-index contact load.

p5_micro_quarantine_flag → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge upward Quarantine removes agents from contact layers, reducing exposure events per remaining edge, so layer incidence per edge can fall when quarantine covers active layer members.

p5_micro_quarantine_flag → p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction upward Quarantining an index case in a household dyad reduces subsequent attributed household exposures, lowering the fraction of dyads with any attributed event.

p5_micro_quarantine_flag → p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio upward More quarantined agents in a layer lower the quarantined group's mean in-layer degree relative to non-quarantined agents, reducing the layer suppression ratio through behavioural withdrawal.

p5_micro_quarantine_flag → p7_meso_layer_exposure_share upward Quarantine changes which layers remain active; settings with many quarantined members lose exposure share while less affected layers gain share.

p5_micro_quarantine_flag → p8_meso_layer_post_trough_incidence_ratio upward Quarantine after the trough can suppress layer-specific resurgence; layers with higher quarantine coverage show lower post-trough incidence ratios.

p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio → p1_meso_band_hazard_dispersion upward If adherence differs by age, quarantine contact reduction is uneven across age bands, widening band-specific exposure hazards and increasing dispersion.

p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge upward Agents with lower quarantine contact ratios contribute fewer layer contacts and exposures, reducing layer incidence per edge when such adherence is common in the layer.

p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio → p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction upward Household dyad members with lower quarantine contact ratios sustain more in-home contact, raising the chance that the dyad accumulates an attributed exposure.

p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio → p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio upward Heterogeneous per-agent contact ratios under quarantine aggregate into the layer-level ratio: agents who reduce contacts more strongly lower the quarantined mean degree, increasing suppression.

p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio → p7_meso_layer_exposure_share upward Adherence differences shift exposure activity from layers where quarantined agents withdraw toward layers where they remain active, changing layer exposure shares.

p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio → p8_meso_layer_post_trough_incidence_ratio upward Higher adherence in a layer suppresses post-trough attributed incidence more than at the trough, lowering that layer's post-trough ratio.

p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta → p6_meso_quarantined_degree_dispersion upward Heterogeneous individual reductions in degree under quarantine create a wider spread of contact degree among quarantined agents.

p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta → p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth upward Agents whose quarantine degree remains close to normal sustain transmission after the trough, increasing aggregate infectious growth.
p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta → p8_macro_resurgence_amplitude upward Heterogeneous adherence leaves some quarantined agents with high contact degree, providing channels for a larger rebound.

p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard upward Quarantined agents who achieve zero contacts contribute no exposures, reducing the exposure hazard in their age band compared with bands where quarantined agents maintain contacts.

p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag → p2_meso_layer_active_run upward Full contact suppression by quarantined agents removes exposure events from their layers, which can break the layer's consecutive active run and shorten its length.

p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count upward A quarantined household member with zero contacts cannot generate secondary exposures in the dyad, lowering the dyad's attributed secondary count.

p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load upward Zero-contact quarantined agents contribute zero degree to the per-index contact load; their presence in the newly quarantined set lowers the layer's average contact load because the average includes these zeros.

p7_micro_exposure_step_index → p7_macro_age_composition_drift upward If later-exposed cohorts have a different age structure from early cohorts, the timing of individual first exposures shifts the aggregate age composition of incident exposures.
p7_micro_exposure_step_index → p7_macro_median_age_of_new_exposures upward Cohort timing changes which age groups contribute new exposures, moving the median age of agents with exposure transitions.
p7_micro_exposure_step_index → p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth upward Exposures occurring later in the run feed the post-trough infectious pool, increasing measured growth after the trough.
p7_micro_exposure_step_index → p8_macro_resurgence_amplitude upward A later distribution of individual first exposures places more new infections after the trough, raising the rebound amplitude.

p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard upward A longer exposure-to-diagnosis interval means the agent remains undetected and potentially infectious for more steps, increasing the number of exposure events generated among susceptible age-band members and raising the band's exposure hazard.

p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval → p2_meso_layer_active_run upward Longer intervals delay diagnosis and isolation, so exposed agents continue contacting others in their layers for more steps, sustaining layer-level exposure activity and lengthening consecutive active runs.

p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count upward In a household dyad, a longer exposure-to-diagnosis interval for the index case provides more time for within-dyad transmission before isolation, increasing the dyad's secondary exposure count.

p8_micro_post_trough_exposure_flag → p7_meso_band_exposure_share upward Post-trough exposure transitions in particular age bands add incident activity after the citywide infectious minimum; if resurgence is age-selective, these late exposures change the band shares of new exposure transitions at subsequent steps.

p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion → p2_macro_layer_incidence_entropy upward Within-layer degree dispersion creates core-periphery contact patterns that make some layers dominate exposure production, changing cross-layer incidence entropy.

p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion → p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth upward Dispersed degree within a layer leaves high-contact agents able to restart transmission after the trough, increasing post-trough infectious growth.
p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion → p8_macro_resurgence_amplitude upward Strong within-layer degree inequality can produce concentrated superspreading events that amplify the post-trough rebound.

p4_meso_group_exposure_yield_silent → p4_macro_silent_prevalence_share upward Quarantine-status groups that generate more exposures per silent infectious person-step expand the silent infectious pool, increasing silent prevalence share.

p4_meso_group_exposure_yield_silent → p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth upward High silent exposure yield in groups after the trough sustains aggregate infectious growth by continuously adding new infections.

p4_meso_group_exposure_yield_silent → p8_macro_resurgence_amplitude upward Groups with high silent exposure yield can drive a larger rebound because their hidden transmission chains remain active through the decline.

p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p4_macro_detection_coverage_rate upward Higher per-edge known-contact incidence in layers brings more infections to diagnosis through tracing, raising new diagnoses per infectious person-step.
p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p5_macro_quarantine_coverage upward Layer-level tracing yield converts more flagged contacts into quarantined agents, increasing population quarantine coverage.
p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p5_macro_known_contact_prevalence upward Higher known-contact incidence per layer edge increases the standing caseload of known contacts at the population level.
p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p8_macro_resurgence_amplitude upward Stronger layer tracing yield removes contacts from transmission chains, reducing the fuel available for a post-trough rebound.

p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p8_macro_resurgence_breadth upward Effective per-edge tracing in some layers suppresses those settings after the trough, reducing the share of layers that show renewed incidence.

p7_meso_band_share_drift → p1_macro_band_attack_range upward When exposure incidence shifts toward particular age bands, cumulative attack ratios diverge further between the most and least affected bands.

p7_meso_band_share_drift → p1_macro_band_composition_mismatch upward Age-band exposure share drift changes the composition of new exposures relative to susceptible person-time, increasing composition mismatch.
p7_meso_band_share_drift → p7_macro_median_age_of_new_exposures upward Drift in age-band shares of exposure transitions changes the weighting of age groups, moving the median age of new exposures.

p7_meso_band_share_drift → p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth upward Drift toward more active or less immune age bands can sustain new infections after the trough, raising aggregate post-trough growth.
p7_meso_band_share_drift → p8_macro_resurgence_amplitude upward A shift in exposure burden toward age bands with more remaining susceptible contacts can amplify the post-trough rebound.

p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio → p1_macro_band_attack_range upward Differential post-trough incidence across age bands widens cumulative attack ratios between the most and least affected bands.

p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio → p1_macro_band_composition_mismatch upward Age-selective post-trough exposure increases alter the exposure composition relative to susceptible person-time, raising composition mismatch.

p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio → p7_macro_age_composition_drift upward When some age bands have higher post-trough incidence ratios than others, the age composition of incident exposures shifts away from its early-run reference.

p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio → p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth upward Age bands with high post-trough exposure rates contribute disproportionately to new infections, increasing aggregate post-trough infectious growth.

p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio → p8_macro_resurgence_amplitude upward Age-selective post-trough increases in exposure rates add to the overall infectious pool, raising the observed resurgence amplitude.

N1 | p1_micro_new_exposure_flag Agent new-exposure transition indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: age_structured_incidence_divergence Definition: X_i(t) = 1 if exposed_i(t) = true and exposed_i(t-1) = false, otherwise 0; defined only when agent i is observed at both step t and the immediately preceding observed step t-1 in the same run; undefined if either observation is missing. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N2 | p1_micro_ever_exposed_state Agent cumulative ever-exposed indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: age_structured_incidence_divergence Definition: E_i(t) = max over observed steps s <= t in the same run of X_i(s), where X is the new-exposure transition indicator; E_i(t) = 1 if any such s has X_i(s) = 1, else 0; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N8 | p2_micro_layer_degree Agent contact degree within a contact layer Scale: micro | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: d_i,l(t) = number of distinct contact records at step t in layer l with agent_id = i plus those with partner_id = i, de-duplicated by unordered pair so that a reciprocal pair counts once; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N9 | p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag Agent exposure transition attributed to a layer Scale: micro | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: E_i,l(t) = 1 if X_i(t) = 1 and the layer recorded on the exposure event for that agent and step equals l; 0 if X_i(t) = 1 and the recorded layer is non-null and different from l; undefined if X_i(t) = 0, if the recorded layer is null, or if no exposure event can be matched. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N10 | p2_micro_layer_beta_load Agent per-layer contact weight load Scale: micro | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: W_i,l(t) = sum of beta over the undirected contact edges at step t in layer l incident to agent i; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N16 | p3_micro_household_degree Agent degree in the persistent household layer Scale: micro | Phenomenon: household_secondary_attack_concentration Definition: d_i,H(t) = number of distinct undirected contact pairs at step t in layer l_H incident to agent i; l_H is the layer value with the largest mean consecutive-step Jaccard overlap of its edge set over all observed steps in the run; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N17 | p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag Agent source-attributed exposure indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: household_secondary_attack_concentration Definition: A_i(t) = 1 if X_i(t) = 1 and the matched exposure event has a non-null partner_id; undefined if X_i(t) = 0 or if the matched event has a null partner_id, since no source can be resolved. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N18 | p3_micro_household_attributed_flag Agent household-attributed exposure indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: household_secondary_attack_concentration Definition: H_i(t) = 1 if A_i(t) = 1 and the layer recorded on that exposure event equals l_H; 0 if A_i(t) = 1 and the layer is non-null and different from l_H; undefined if A_i(t) is undefined. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N24 | p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag Agent silent-infectious indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: silent_transmission_masking Definition: Z_i(t) = 1 if infectious_i(t) = true and diagnosed_i(t) = false; 0 if infectious_i(t) = true and diagnosed_i(t) = true; undefined if infectious_i(t) = false or the agent is not observed at t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N25 | p4_micro_silent_infectious_duration Agent cumulative silent-infectious duration Scale: micro | Phenomenon: silent_transmission_masking Definition: D_i(t) = number of observed steps s <= t in the same run with Z_i(s) = 1; undefined if agent i is not observed at t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N26 | p4_micro_symptomatic_undiagnosed_flag Agent symptomatic-but-undiagnosed indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: silent_transmission_masking Definition: Y_i(t) = 1 if symptomatic_i(t) = true and diagnosed_i(t) = false; 0 if symptomatic_i(t) = true and diagnosed_i(t) = true; undefined if symptomatic_i(t) = false or the agent is not observed. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N33 | p5_micro_known_contact_flag Agent known-contact state indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: tracing_capacity_saturation Definition: K_i(t) = 1 if known_contact_i(t) = true, 0 if known_contact_i(t) = false; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N34 | p5_micro_tracing_latency Agent known-contact to quarantine latency Scale: micro | Phenomenon: tracing_capacity_saturation Definition: Tau_i = date_quarantined_i - date_known_contact_i for agent i, defined only when both native dates are non-null for that agent in the run; undefined otherwise. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N35 | p5_micro_quarantine_flag Agent quarantine state indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: tracing_capacity_saturation Definition: Q_i(t) = 1 if quarantined_i(t) = true, 0 if quarantined_i(t) = false; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N43 | p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio Agent contact degree ratio in and out of quarantine Scale: micro | Phenomenon: adherence_heterogeneity_feedback Definition: rho_i = (mean over observed steps s with quarantined_i(s) = true of d_i(s)) / (mean over observed steps s with quarantined_i(s) = false of d_i(s)); undefined when either step set is empty or the non-quarantine mean is 0. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N44 | p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta Agent absolute contact-degree change under quarantine Scale: micro | Phenomenon: adherence_heterogeneity_feedback Definition: delta_i = (mean over observed steps with quarantined_i = true of d_i) - (mean over observed steps with quarantined_i = false of d_i); undefined when either step set is empty. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N45 | p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag Agent full-contact-suppression indicator under quarantine Scale: micro | Phenomenon: adherence_heterogeneity_feedback Definition: Z_i(t) = 1 if quarantined_i(t) = true and d_i(t) = 0; 0 if quarantined_i(t) = true and d_i(t) > 0; undefined if quarantined_i(t) = false or the agent is not observed at t.
